questions.q: What is the main source of cost efficiency in central serving that edge serving cannot replicate?
options: Edge devices are always faster than datacenter GPUs
Batching requests from many different users together on a shared pool of GPUs
Central serving requires no network connection at all
Central serving eliminates the need for any load balancing
questions.explain: Central serving can batch many users' requests together on shared GPUs, driving utilization up. Each edge device only serves its own local requests, so that cross-user batching advantage isn't available.

questions.q: Why does edge serving almost always involve a smaller, more heavily quantized model than central serving?
options: Smaller models are always required by law for on-device deployment
Edge hardware (phones, local gateways) is far more memory- and compute-constrained than a datacenter GPU
Quantization only works on edge devices, never in a datacenter
Edge serving never needs a model at all
questions.explain: Edge devices have much less memory and compute than datacenter GPUs, which forces the deployed model to be smaller and more compressed, creating a real quality ceiling compared to central serving.

questions.q: Which benefit does edge serving provide 'by construction' compared to central serving?
options: Higher GPU utilization than any central pool
Privacy — since inference runs on the device, sensitive data never has to leave it to reach a model
Unlimited model size with no hardware constraints
Guaranteed lower cost per request in every scenario
questions.explain: Because the model runs on or near the device itself, data doesn't need to travel to a remote server to be processed, which is a structural privacy advantage edge serving has over central serving.

questions.q: In a hybrid edge/central architecture, what typically triggers escalation from the edge model to the central model?
options: Every single request is always escalated regardless of outcome
The edge model being uncertain about its answer, or the request needing a larger model's quality
The device running out of battery
Escalation only happens on weekends
questions.explain: A hybrid design typically handles common, latency-critical requests locally and escalates to a central service when the edge model is uncertain or the task needs more capability than the local model has.

questions.q: How is hybrid edge/central routing structurally similar to the cascade routing pattern from Lesson 26?
options: They are unrelated concepts with no structural similarity
Both try a cheaper/faster tier first and escalate to a more capable tier only when needed — hybrid routing just splits the tiers by physical location instead of model size alone
Cascade routing always runs on edge devices only
Hybrid routing never escalates to a second tier
questions.explain: Both patterns try the lighter option first and escalate only when necessary. Hybrid edge/central routing applies that same idea across physical locations rather than just across model sizes in one datacenter.
